subject: general
question: Which state among the following is the largest producer of coffee?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karnataka** is the **largest producer of coffee**.
 
• With **203,445 MT** of coffee output in 2019-20, the state produced over** 70% of India's total coffee production**.
 
• Karnataka's major coffee variety is Robusta, however, the state also produces a limited amount of Arabica.
 
• The state has ideal climatic conditions for coffee plantations, including high altitude, sloppy mountains, and adequate rainfall.
 
• The coffee plantation is located in the Karnataka districts of Chikkamagaluru, Hassan, and Kodagu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Coffee cultivation** in India dates back to the 16th-century Sufi mystic Baba Budan, who returned from Yemen with "seven seeds" of "Mocha" coffee beans and planted them on "Baba Budan Giris" in Karnataka.
 
• Coffee plantations gradually spread over south India, and commercial coffee plantations began in the 18th century.
 
• Coffee is grown mostly in the southern Indian states of **Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is also grown in India's northeastern states.
